text: Git is a popular version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. When working on a project, you often create a feature branch to develop something new without affecting the main code. Once your work is finished, you can merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, many teams use pull requests so that others can review the changes and give feedback. This workflow keeps the project organized and reduces mistakes. Learning how to use branches, merging, and pull requests is an important step for anyone who wants to work effectively with other developers.
